 Mr. Kalidas Surve, Api, Unit-3, G.C.-3, Eow, Mumbai, present

** *
 Coram : M. M. Sathaye, J.
 Dated : 2nd September 202
 P.C.:
1.
Heard learned advocate for Applicant and learned APP for the State.

2. The application seeks pre-arrest bail in connection with C.R.No.147/2019 registered with Byculla Police Station, Mumbai for offences punishable under sections 406, 409, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471,
120-B of the Indian Penal Code.
FIR is dated 08.06.2019.
3. At the outset it is noted that the Applicant is not named in the FIR.
The allegations in the FIR are of siphoning of fixed-deposit (FD) amounts invested by Mumbai Lokhand Va Polad Kamgar Mandal of which the complainant was the Chairman at the relevant time.

entities.text: Mumbai Lokhand Va Polad Kamgar Mandal
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is alleged that Mandal had invested about Rs.45.00 Crore under seven Fds in SBI, Mazgaon Circle Branch, out of which amount to the tune of Rs.36.00 Crore was transferred or withdrawn without instructions or application from the Mandal, which is main allegation of siphoning of funds.
The FIR names the main accused 53.ABA.2124.2023-C.doc Bank-Manager Mr. Nikhil Roy.

1 4.

entities.text: Rakesh Daylal Upadhyay vs The State Of Maharashtra on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It appears that during the investigation, the name of the present Applicant surfaced on the basis of the statement of a co-accused Mr. Manish More and Prashant Chavan.
Co-accused Manish More was arrested and during investigation the Applicant's name surfaced.

On the basis of statement of the co-accused, it is the case of the prosecution that the main accused Nikhil Roy was harbored by the Applicant in his house at Ghodbandar, Thane and that the Applicant was moving around with main accused Nikhil Roy at various places when the main accused was absconding.

5. According to prosecution, first aspect connecting the Applicant with the present crime seems to be Rs.38,16,756/- received by Applicant from the co-accused - Manish More and Rs. 50,000/- from co-accused Prashant Chavan through bank transfers.

Another aspect connecting the Applicant to the present crime, according to prosecution, is that one company by name 'Zapo Limited' has been registered in the name of Applicant and its registration fees are paid by the co-accused - Mr. Manish More from the ill- gotten money.
It is submitted by learned APP that this company established in Mauritius.

6. Learned Counsel for the Applicant submitted that when the Applicant attended the concerned Police Station / reported to the concerned Investigating Officer, he has already explained that though the said company is registered in his name, he was told by the co-accused - Prashant Chavan and Manish More that he will be given 10% profit from the profits of the company and therefore he had given his documents by email.

According to the Applicant, he and co-accused - Manish More were good friends and were 53.ABA.2124.2023-C.doc having transactions for helping each other financially and the Applicant is not connected with the ill-gotten money, which is alleged to have been received from the account of Manish More.
The Applicant has already submitted his bank statements with the investigating agency.
7. Admittedly, as per this Court's order dated 10.06.2025, the Applicant has reported to concerned Investigation Officer on 3 dates and supplied information.

The alleged involvement of the Applicant in harboring the main accused Nikhil Roy or roaming around with him, when Mr. Roy was absconding, it is based purely on the statement of co-accused-Mr. Manish More who was in custody.
Admittedly, all other accused in crime are on regular bail.

8. So far as two antecedents pointed out by learned APP (CR No. 38 of 2020, registered with Amboli Police Station, Mumbai under section 376, 328, 342 r/w. 34 of IPC and C.R. 616 of 2022 registered with Kashimira Police Station, under sections 420 r/w. 34 of IPC) are concerned, it is submitted that the Applicant is on anticipatory/regular bail respectively.
In C.R. No. 38 of 2020, the sections invoked are completely different.
Copies of orders dated 04.09.2020 and 23.09.2022 are produced on record.
This position is not seriously disputed by learned APP.

9. In the aforesaid facts and circumstances and considering the nature of allegations, extent of involvement and its basis and co-operation of Applicant, as explained above, and further considering the fact that the Applicant is already protected by order of this Court dated 28/07/2023,
case for grant of this Application is made out.

Hence, the following order:

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (a) The Anticipatory Bail Application is allowed in terms of order dated 28/07/2023 and is subjected to same terms 53.ABA.2124.2023-C.doc and conditions mentioned therein.
(b) In addition, the Applicant (Rakesh Daylal Upadhyay) is directed co-operate with the investigation by reporting as and when required, on sufficient notice.
10. Anticipatory Bail Application disposed of in above terms.

(M. M. SATHAYE, J.)
